task.title: Reconciliation with incomplete ancestry
task.specification: config={} . Start local head=null and an empty immutable record graph. Events {head:null|string,records:[{id:string,parent:null|string,value:integer}]}. IDs cannot parent themselves; supplied records form an acyclic graph. Merge records atomically: if any known or within-event ID disagrees in parent/value, reject the whole event with decision=conflict and keep graph/head. Otherwise add them, even when parents are missing. Walk parent links from local and remote head until null or an unknown ID. If heads equal, decision=same. If local head occurs in the known remote chain (including terminal null), set local head=remote head and decision=advance. Else if remote head occurs in the local chain, decision=ahead. Else if both walks reach null, decision=fork. Otherwise decision=unknown. Output {head,decision,missing}; missing is sorted distinct unknown terminal IDs from BOTH walks performed before any head advance. For rejected records compute missing from the unchanged graph and the requested remote head. No value or clock similarity establishes ancestry. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Dendrochronology
matchedCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
matchedCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
matchedCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

shuffledCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
shuffledCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
shuffledCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

initial.explanation: The conditional rule is ancestry reconciliation over a persistent record graph: commit records atomically, walk both heads through known parents, report unknown terminal IDs, and classify equality, advancement, being ahead, fork, or unresolved ancestry. A conflicting batch is rejected without mutation, but its missing set is computed against the unchanged graph.
initial.mapping: Local variables map to the contract as follows: state.head is the local head; state.records is the immutable known ID-to-record graph; event.head is the remote head; event.records is the proposed atomic merge; output.head and output.decision report the resulting local head and relation; output.missing reports unknown walk terminals.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal JSON and graph constraints. JavaScript strings are compared by Unicode scalar values using an explicit code-point comparator, not UTF-16 ordering.

final.explanation: Reconciles each remote event against the persistent local graph. Records are validated for conflicts before any mutation; conflicting events preserve both graph and head. Valid records are merged atomically, then both ancestry walks are performed on the merged graph. Unknown terminal IDs are deduplicated and sorted by Unicode code point order. Classification follows equality, remote advancement, local advancement, fork, or unresolved ancestry, while only advancement changes the local head.

initial.explanation: Track an immutable record graph and local head. Merge each event atomically, reject conflicting IDs, then compare the two parent walks. Unknown terminal IDs are collected from both walks before any advance.
initial.mapping: Records map IDs to immutable {parent,value} identities; parent links define ancestry. Local and remote heads are compared by graph reachability, never by values or timing.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal-value, acyclicity, and size constraints. Duplicate identical records are harmless; conflicting duplicates reject the complete event.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x!=='object'||!['same','advance','ahead','fork','unknown','conflict'].includes(x.decision)||!Array.isArray(x.missing)||!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(x,'head'))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{head:null,records:[]};let old=s.records, conflict=false, add=[];for(const r of event.records){let prior=null;for(const x of old)if(x.id===r.id){prior=x;break}for(const x of add)if(x.id===r.id){prior=x;break}if(prior&&(prior.parent!==r.parent||prior.value!==r.value)){conflict=true;break}if(!prior)add.push({id:r.id,parent:r.parent,value:r.value})}let rec=conflict?old:old.concat(add);function get(id){for(const r of rec)if(r.id===id)return r;return null}function walk(h){let a=[],m=[],x=h;while(x!==null){a.push(x);let r=get(x);if(!r){m.push(x);break}x=r.parent}a.push(null);return{a,m}}let L=walk(s.head),R=walk(event.head),missing=L.m.concat(R.m);missing.sort();let u=[];for(const x of missing)if(!u.length||u[u.length-1]!==x)u.push(x);let decision,head=s.head;if(conflict)decision='conflict';else if(s.head===event.head)decision='same';else if(L.a.indexOf(event.head)>=0)decision='ahead';else if(R.a.indexOf(s.head)>=0){head=event.head;decision='advance'}else if(L.a[L.a.length-1]===null&&R.a[R.a.length-1]===null)decision='fork';else decision='unknown';return{state:{head,records:rec},output:{head,decision,missing:u}}}

final.explanation: Maintain the local head and an immutable record graph. Each event is merged atomically: conflicting definitions reject all additions. Compare parent walks using the graph before any head advance, collect distinct terminal unknown IDs, and apply ancestry rules in the specified direction.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{head:null,records:[]},old=s.records,add=[],bad=false;for(let z of event.records){let p=null;for(let r of old)if(r.id===z.id){p=r;break}for(let r of add)if(r.id===z.id){p=r;break}if(p){if(p.parent!==z.parent||p.value!==z.value){bad=true;break}}else add.push({id:z.id,parent:z.parent,value:z.value})}let rs=bad?old:old.concat(add);function get(id){for(let r of rs)if(r.id===id)return r;return null}function walk(h){let a=[],m=[],x=h;while(x!==null){a.push(x);let r=get(x);if(!r){m.push(x);break}x=r.parent}a.push(null);return[a,m]}let L=walk(s.head),R=walk(event.head),mm=L[1].concat(R[1]);mm.sort();let missing=[];for(let x of mm)if(!missing.length||missing[missing.length-1]!==x)missing.push(x);let head=s.head,decision;if(bad)decision='conflict';else if(s.head===event.head)decision='same';else if(R[0].indexOf(s.head)>=0){head=event.head;decision='advance'}else if(L[0].indexOf(event.head)>=0)decision='ahead';else if(L[0][L[0].length-1]===null&&R[0][R[0].length-1]===null)decision='fork';else decision='unknown';return{state:{head,records:rs},output:{head,decision,missing}}}

initial.explanation: Use the supplied comparator idea only as optional assistance: retain the local head unless the ancestry relation proves remote advancement. No threshold or hysteresis behavior is part of this task.
initial.mapping: The local head is retained state; records are immutable identity/value/parent facts. A remote head is accepted only through exact ancestry after atomic record validation.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal-value constraints. Missing IDs terminate each walk, and missing output is the sorted union of both terminal unknown IDs.

final.explanation: Retain the local head unless the remote head is proven to descend from it. Records are merged atomically; conflicting identities reject the event while ancestry and missing-ID calculations use the unchanged graph. Missing terminal IDs from both pre-advance walks are deduplicated and sorted by Unicode code-point order.
